Turing instability: linear growth and small-amplitude patterns Use a matrix exponential to validate stable homogeneous kinetics and diffusion-driven growth of a selected Schnakenberg mode. Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless a=0.1,b=0.9, equilibrium(1,0.9), diffusivities(0.01,1), periodic k=2 and initial amplitude1e-4. Restrict runs to linear t=1 and nonlinear t=4. Adopted numerical method Advance the linearized and short nonlinear PDEs using original centered differences/RK4. Record mode amplitudes/growth on three grids, minimum concentrations and early-pattern amplification. ut=Duuxx+a−u+u2v,vt=Dvvxx+b−u2vut​=Du​uxx​+a−u+u2v,vt​=Dv​vxx​+b−u2v ∂tδz^=(J−k2D)δz^,δz^(t)=e(J−k2D)tδz^(0)∂t​δz=(J−k2D)δz,δz(t)=e(J−k2D)tδz(0) References and measured quantities Compare linear numerical fields with SciPy expm of continuum J-k²D and measure spatial convergence.
